_readme: Single config for automation/. The only place where file names, column names, category names, evidence keywords and assumptions live. Edit here, never in the .py files.

tickets._file_pattern_note: Glob in the data folder. If several files match, the last by name is used and the others are listed in the output.
tickets._optional_columns_note: Keys from columns. A file without these still runs: the flags that depend on them are skipped and the report says so. All other columns are required.

known_categories.Thumbnail re-upload: Reply with the self-serve thumbnail replacement link
known_categories.Tax form (W-9/W-8): Human: chase or check the tax form
known_categories.Payout question: Human: answer from the payout records
known_categories.Login issue: Human: reset or unblock the login

pilot._note: Read only when the ticket file has this column, which the Q1 bundle file does not. It is our proposed contract for the pilot export: the ticketing tool must record, per target ticket, whether the self-serve path resolved it or it came back to a person. Values are matched ignoring case.

fixture_marker.banner: The figures below demonstrate the method. They are not a Northwind result.
fixture_marker._note: A demo input is recognised by any of three signals, so the label survives if one is lost: line 1 of the marker file, the provenance column on each row, or the ticket ID prefix. Both reports, stdout and the routed queue then say so. A file that mixes synthetic and real rows fails pilot acceptance.

assumptions._max_plausible_minutes_note: ASSUMPTION: one ticket cannot take more than one 8 hour work day. Rows above this go to EXCEPTION and their minutes are not counted.
assumptions._pilot_days_note: ASSUMPTION: the two week pilot named in BUILDER_SPEC.md. Override with --pilot-days.

candidates.find: brand-deal|three-way match|month-end reconciliation|three are: the CRM
needed: CRM deal export, one row per closed deal: deal ID, brand, close date, deal amount, currency
Invoicing sheet, one row per invoice: invoice ID, deal ID, invoice date, billed amount, currency
Payout tracker, one row per creator payout: payout ID, deal ID, creator ID, payout date, payout amount, split percent
A time log of the close, one row per day worked: date, task, hours (to turn the self-reported days into a measured before figure)
The written list of manual steps that the finance review assigns as an action item
candidates.why_not: Strongest claim, but self-reported with no time log, and the CRM export, invoicing sheet and payout tracker are not in the bundle. Building it here would mean inventing the data it reconciles.
candidates.provenance: All of them trace to one person's self-report (the finance analyst who does the work): her own Slack messages, the finance review she scribed, and the CFO repeating the figure at the leadership sync. No time log for it is in the bundle.

candidates.workflow: Creator support queue, all categories together
candidates.why_not: This is the measurement behind the category rows, not a single workflow.

candidates.area: Ops and support (also touches Content post team)
candidates.find: thumbnail|every swap|low dollar value per ticket

needed: Form status per creator (requested, returned, valid) and creator contact data, to drive an automatic chaser
candidates.why_not: The log carries no form status or creator contact data to drive a chaser, the work needs a compliance check per form, and the reply in the same thread points to cheap off-the-shelf services and defers it to Q3 planning. The router can be pointed at it with --category.

candidates.workflow: SaaS line checks at close (duplicate lines, currency, contract versus posted)
candidates.find: double-count|entered twice|normalize to USD|against what's posted
needed: Any statement of time spent, plus vendor invoices and contracts
candidates.why_not: No time figure anywhere in the bundle.

needed: Any volume or effort data for post-production: jobs per week, hours per job, queue length
candidates.why_not: Called the bottleneck, with no volume or effort data in the bundle.

pick_reasons.text: The ops lead asks for exactly this automation by name.
Each request is the same manual re-export and re-upload (cited). That it needs no money or compliance decision, so a rule can route it safely, is our judgment and not a sourced fact.
